clue.text: Cheese representative beset by a spiteful woman

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the representative sits inside the spiteful woman

parts.note: cat is slang for a spiteful, catty woman
a member, as of Parliament, represents constituents

explanation.surface: An MP is surrounded by a vindictive woman at a cheese counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft, white-rinded French cheese from Normandy, a classic example of the type.

clue.text: Agreeing with many 'over boy worker

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
on and over can both mean resting upon
a son is a boy
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A boy employee agrees with many over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant with means in harmony or in agreement with.

clue.text: Border sheep for example to be raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising each word turns it upwards, so each piece reads backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep on the border is to be brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be raised' turns RAM into MAR and EG into GE, each in place.
explanation.definitionFit: An old or poetic word for a margin or edge.

clue.text: Not a generous period for an interval

parts.note: mean means stingy, not generous
time means a period

explanation.surface: A stingy stretch for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The time between two events is the intervening period.

clue.text: In service uniform, put on an air

indicators.note: put on means one piece is added to the other, here the first above the second

parts.note: uniform means even, regular
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Dress in uniform and assume an affected manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on an air' suggests pretending; in this down entry 'put on' places EVEN over SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening prayer service, a religious service.

clue.text: It's a new way to obtain non-alcoholic drink

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
a way is a direction, here E for east

explanation.surface: A fresh method for getting a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An herbal tea, an infusion drunk without alcohol.

clue.text: Grave seen right inside a grotto

indicators.note: inside places the letter for right within the word for a grotto

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

explanation.surface: A tomb is discovered in a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a noun, a tomb, but it is the verb meaning to engrave or cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To grave is an old verb for engraving, cutting letters or figures into stone or wood.

clue.text: Artist enters a bistro for a bottle

indicators.note: enters means the artist goes inside the bistro

parts.note: a bistro is a small café
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's artist

explanation.surface: A painter goes into a small restaurant for a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass flask used to serve wine or water at table.

clue.text: Upset a porter — be' a baddie!

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A villain is told to annoy a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or scoundrel, an unprincipled person.

clue.text: The editor accepts staff as being correct

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the editor contains the staff

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
men are a workforce or staff

explanation.surface: An editor approves employees as being right.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to remove errors from a text, to put it right.

clue.text: Set forth but rushed back with speed

indicators.note: back tells us the word for rushed is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: rushed means ran
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone set off, then hurried back fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set forth' looks like departing, but here it means to relate or recount; 'back' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth a story is to tell or recount it in order.

clue.text: Does it weigh much on one's conscience?

definitions.text: Does it weigh much on one's conscience?

parts.words: Does it weigh much on one's conscience?
parts.note: the word is both a moral qualm that troubles the conscience and a tiny apothecaries' weight of twenty grains, so it hardly weighs much

explanation.surface: A question about how heavily guilt presses on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains that also names a moral hesitation or qualm.

clue.text: It's clear round the green

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A golfer remarks on a clear view around the putting green.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is heraldry's word for green, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open and plainly visible, not hidden, is clear to all.

clue.text: A certain coolness drags on if improperly dealt with

indicators.note: letters handled improperly are mixed up, like cards badly dealt

explanation.surface: A calm attitude persists if things are mishandled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly dealt with' rearranges DRAGSONIF into the French phrase for cold blood.
explanation.definitionFit: French for cold blood, it means composure and calmness under pressure.

clue.text: A Liberal preparing to do battle is redoubtable

parts.note: arming means equipping oneself for battle

explanation.surface: A politician readying for a fight is a formidable figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something fearsome that inspires dread or fright.

clue.text: One thousand involved in a race for life

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so these letters go inside the race

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand runners take part in a race for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a contest but means a people, A NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness, vitality or being alive.

clue.text: Just for fun!

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is done simply for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just or equitable, and a fair is a funfair with rides and amusements.

clue.text: Nice reeds for building a nest

indicators.note: for building means the letters are assembled into something new

explanation.surface: Birds use good reeds to construct a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a home or dwelling place.

clue.text: He'll move the ordinary seaman : into decent surroundings

indicators.note: into places the seaman within the next word
surroundings means the decent word encloses the seaman

parts.note: proper means decent, respectable
OS is the abbreviation for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: Someone moves a sailor into respectable quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' means to propose a motion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: At a meeting, the one who moves a motion puts it forward for debate.

clue.text: Free from engagements, the dunderhead cut down on food

parts.note: the head of dunder is its first letter, D
ate less means reduced eating

explanation.surface: A fool on a diet has no dates in the diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool, but read as dunder plus head it gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no social appointments or romantic dates.

clue.text: Thrice-married corporal

parts.note: tri- is the prefix meaning three times

explanation.surface: A soldier who has wed three times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporal' looks like the army rank but is the adjective meaning bodily: trim describes the body's physical condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means relating to the body, and trim describes a body in good physical shape.

clue.text: Extends a means of access into the mountains

indicators.note: into puts the means of access inside the mountains

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a way of getting to a place

explanation.surface: Building a road into the hills widens reach.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to make it larger or extend its scope.

clue.text: Burn in anger, but sign it eventually

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the run of words

explanation.surface: Someone flares up angrily but will sign in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight or catch fire.

clue.text: Find a way round some wood in the West Country

indicators.note: round means the way goes around the wood

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for ..., a way
a tree gives wood

explanation.surface: Seek a path around a copse in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: STREET is a large village in Somerset, a county in England's south-west (the West Country).
explanation.definitionFit: Street is a place in Somerset, home of Clarks shoes.

clue.text: Flighty creature operating in a disorganised way

indicators.note: disorganised letters are jumbled out of their order

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained person works chaotically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a disorganised way' rearranges OPERATING; 'Flighty' suggests a giddy person, but this creature literally flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A British butterfly whose male has bright tips on its forewings, a creature of flight.

clue.text: No longer in the minority

parts.note: suggests not a small group, but means no longer under the legal adult threshold

explanation.surface: A group that has stopped being outnumbered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being an adult, legally past one's minority.

clue.text: Note: leave water for an animal

parts.note: E is a musical note
to land is to come ashore from the water

explanation.surface: A memo telling someone to get out of the water to meet a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African antelope, a kind of animal.

clue.text: The musician's very very good under a foolish leader

indicators.note: under means this piece sits below the other in the down entry

parts.note: an ass is a fool
A1 means first-class

explanation.surface: An excellent player under a silly conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian musical term for very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: A fall from grace in the Orient appears senseless

parts.note: a sin is a fall from grace
taken as written
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A disgrace in the Far East looks pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean foolish or stupid, lacking good sense.

clue.text: Oddly, no — test's ' required, though it's worn out

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange way, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A strange result: no examination is needed though something is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges NOTESTS; 'worn out' looks like exhausted but means worn outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy hat, a broad-brimmed headgear worn outdoors.

clue.text: He takes the queen's letters after mid-morning, that is

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, are the queen's initials
the middle letter of morning is N

explanation.surface: A man collects the royal post just after breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks winning Premium Bond numbers in Britain, hence 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment, a computer personified as a man, draws British Premium Bond prizes.

clue.text: Revolver found in the entrance!

parts.note: suggests a gun found at a doorway, but means a rotating gate that people push through one at a time

explanation.surface: A gun discovered at a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating barrier with arms at a gate that admits people one by one.
